headline: High: Copilot can ingest repo context and propose edits while Airbyte has broad egress, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk if paired on shared business data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads editor open buffers and repo context by default, so malicious content in files can influence its outputs. Airbyte has broad network egress and can move data through pipelines, but no shared clipboard/MCP is documented. The interaction is plausible via shared files, not proven impossible, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes attacker-controlled text into files that Copilot later reads as repo context
IF the pair is run on a shared workspace where file contents are treated as trusted instructions
mitigations: Restrict Copilot to reviewed branches only
Separate Airbyte output directories from Copilot workspaces
Add a prompt-injection lint step for generated files
Disable automatic application of Copilot Workspace edits
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for pipeline-generated files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Copilot sends context to api.githubcopilot.com and reads repo/open-buffer content. If business data lands in shared files or buffers, Copilot can transmit it off-host. That makes leakage a default-dangerous pathway with potentially irreversible exfiltration.
conditions: IF business data is written into repo files or editor buffers visible to Copilot
IF Copilot is allowed to process those buffers while Airbyte outputs sensitive records
mitigations: Keep business data out of repos opened in Copilot
Use a redacted staging dataset for Airbyte
Turn off Copilot on sensitive workspaces
Limit Airbyte outputs to non-sensitive sinks
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on editor buffers and pipeline outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can move data over the network, while Copilot can write files and modify git state. Their write surfaces overlap on the same repository or workspace, but Copilot's concurrency model says shared state with other instances is none beyond editor buffers, so conflict is plausible yet not clearly high. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Airbyte-generated artifacts and Copilot edits target the same directory
IF git state is modified by Copilot Workspace while Airbyte jobs also write files
mitigations: Use separate branches for Airbyte and Copilot work
Lock the repo during automated Airbyte runs
Review Copilot edits before merge
Keep Airbyte outputs outside the source tree
requires-engineering: add file-level locking around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace proposes edits for human review, but it also consumes repo context that may include Airbyte-produced artifacts. If Airbyte outputs incorrect data or schema changes, Copilot can propagate them into code or docs without independent verification. The human review step reduces but does not eliminate the cascade.
conditions: IF Airbyte emits incorrect schema or transformed data into repo-visible files
IF Copilot uses those files as authoritative context for edits
mitigations: Require schema validation before Copilot edits
Review Airbyte outputs before exposing them to Copilot
Pin generated artifacts to known-good snapshots
Add tests that fail on unexpected pipeline output
requires-engineering: add automated verification between Airbyte and Copilot

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte is a data-engineering system touching business data, while Copilot is a closed-source cloud service with GitHub repo-context OAuth and vendor-only egress. If regulated business data is placed into Copilot-visible files, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profile lacks explicit residency details, so uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated business data is stored in files or buffers accessible to Copilot
IF organizational policy requires local-only processing or stricter retention than GitHub Copilot provides
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Copilot workspaces
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Review vendor retention terms before enabling Copilot
Separate compliance-sensitive repos from Copilot-enabled repos
requires-engineering: implement policy-based workspace segmentation
